tool_input.paragraphs:
["The overall credibility check result is Fail, so the results of step s_combo1 (static, combination combo1) should not be treated as converged or reliable. The reaction balance check passed, meaning the applied loads are balanced by the support reactions.","The maximum von Mises stress, excluding the constrained faces, is {{s_combo1.vm_max_mpa}}, against a material yield strength of {{s_combo1.strength_mpa}}. However, the stress convergence check failed: the maximum stress increases with each refinement, from {{s_combo1.conv2.level0}} on the first mesh to {{s_combo1.conv2.level1}} on the second and {{s_combo1.conv2.level2}} on the third. This pattern suggests a stress singularity (such as a sharp corner or point load), so this stress value cannot be used as a design basis.","The maximum displacement is {{s_combo1.u_max_mm}}. The displacement convergence check passed: the values across the three meshes ({{s_combo1.conv3.level0}}, {{s_combo1.conv3.level1}}, {{s_combo1.conv3.level2}}) differ very little.","The mesh quality check is Unknown. Raising the second-order elements on curved surfaces made them too distorted, so straight-edged second-order elements were used, with curved surfaces approximated by chords. Stresses near curved surfaces may therefore deviate noticeably.","No safety factor is given, because the credibility checks did not pass (overall result: Fail). The analysis is linear elastic with small deformation, with no contact, residual stress or surface hardening. Stresses near constrained and loaded faces come from idealized boundary conditions, and these regions were excluded when evaluating the maximum stress."],
"suggestions": ["Have an engineer identify the sharp corner or point-load location that drives the rising maximum stress, and check whether it is a real geometric feature or a modeling artifact.","Add a fillet at the sharp corner, or replace the point load with a distributed load, if that matches the real condition, then rerun the stress convergence study.","Refine the mesh on curved surfaces so that several element layers span the curvature, and then recheck mesh quality.","Locally refine the mesh around the suspected singularity and check whether the stress there stabilizes. If it keeps rising, evaluate the stress with a method that does not depend on the singular point, such as a hot-spot or section-averaged approach.","Rerun all credibility checks after the model changes, and only then consider a safety factor evaluation."]
